Recruiter I've known for 8 years just sent me the breakdown from her Q1 pipeline

Average SaaS role: 2,847 applications. Up from 312 in Q1 2023

Their ATS auto-rejects 94% before human eyes see them. Keywords like "bootcamp" or "career change" = instant rejection

"AI screening" means offshore contractors in Manila clicking through resumes for $4/hour while the AI badge makes it sound sophisticated

She's placing 11 people this quarter. Same period last year was 89

The roles that do exist? "AI Engineer" paying $95K for what used to be $180K senior positions. Requires PhD-level ML knowledge for work that's basically writing API calls to OpenAI

New grad success rate is 0.8%. Not 8%. Less than 1%

Bootcamp grads are completely radioactive. HR sees that certificate and assumes you're desperate enough to work for peanuts

Mid-level engineers (3-7 years) have the worst outlook. Too expensive for junior work, not senior enough to "leverage AI effectively"

Companies posting "we're hiring" for show while their actual headcount planning shows 40% workforce reduction by Q4

The few offers going out? 60% are bait-and-switch contract positions disguised as FTE roles
